title_en: Liu Zhichao v. Tongfang CNKI (Beijing) Technology Co., Ltd. — dispute over a sales contract
ruling_gist_en: The minimum top-up amount clause unilaterally set by a business operator not only infringes upon consumers' right of free choice and unjustly occupies consumers' funds, but also additionally increases the burden on consumers when applying for a refund. Therefore, this minimum top-up amount clause is a standard term that restricts consumers' legitimate rights and interests, constituting unfair and unreasonable provisions for consumers, and should be deemed invalid.

full_text_en:
Liu Zhichao v. Tongfang CNKI (Beijing) Technology Co., Ltd. — Dispute over Sales Contract

【Ruling Summary】

The minimum top-up amount clause unilaterally set by an operator not only infringes upon consumers' right to free choice and occupies consumers' funds without cause, but also additionally increases consumers' burden when applying for a refund. Therefore, such a minimum top-up amount clause constitutes a standard term that restricts consumers' legitimate rights and interests, is an unfair and unreasonable provision for consumers, and shall be deemed invalid.

Plaintiff: Liu Zhichao, male, 20 years old, Han ethnicity, residing in Gusu District, Suzhou, Jiangsu Province.

Defendant: Tongfang CNKI (Beijing) Technology Co., Ltd., domiciled at Xixiaokou Road, Haidian District, Beijing.
Legal Representative: Wang Mingliang, Chairman of the Company.

Plaintiff Liu Zhichao filed a lawsuit with the Gusu District People's Court of Suzhou, Jiangsu Province, against Defendant Tongfang CNKI (Beijing) Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Tongfang CNKI) regarding a dispute over a sales contract.

Plaintiff Liu Zhichao alleged: When the plaintiff downloaded a document titled "Traditional Chinese Medicine" on China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI) operated by the defendant, a webpage prompted that a fee of 7 yuan was required. After the plaintiff clicked the "Purchase" button, a top-up page appeared. The plaintiff then entered the "Top-Up Center" of CNKI. The Top-Up Center provided different top-up methods such as Alipay, WeChat Pay, and UnionPay Online, but all set a minimum top-up amount limit, i.e., the minimum top-up limit for individual users was 50 yuan. The plaintiff was forced to top up 50 yuan in order to download the 7-yuan document. After purchasing the document, the plaintiff communicated with customer service regarding the refund of the account balance, but customer service refused to process the refund on the grounds that a handling fee was required for the refund and the refund procedure was complicated and time-consuming. Article 19 of the "Answers to Readers" section on the CNKI webpage states: "The top-up amount cannot be refunded. The purchased top-up amount has no time limit and must be used up." It expressly provides that refunds are not allowed. According to Article 26, paragraph 2 of the Law on the Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests, operators shall not, by way of standard terms, notices, declarations, shop notices, etc., make provisions that exclude or restrict consumers' rights, reduce or exempt operators' liabilities, increase consumers' responsibilities, or are otherwise unfair or unreasonable to consumers, nor shall they use standard terms and technical means to compel transactions. Paragraph 3 of that Article provides that standard terms, notices, declarations, etc., containing the content listed in the preceding paragraph shall be invalid. The provisions on the minimum top-up amount limit and the non-refundability of top-up amounts are standard terms that restrict the plaintiff's rights and increase the plaintiff's responsibilities, and should be invalid. Furthermore, Articles 9 and 10 of the Law on the Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests also stipulate that consumers have the right to free choice and fair trade. The defendant's act of refusing to provide its goods to the plaintiff by setting a minimum top-up amount limit is a conduct imposing unfair and unreasonable transaction conditions to compel transactions, infringing upon the plaintiff's aforementioned rights. Therefore, the plaintiff requested the court to: 1. Revoke the minimum top-up amount limit set by the defendant; 2. Order the defendant to refund the full balance of 43 yuan in the plaintiff's account; 3. Order the defendant to bear the litigation costs. During the proceedings, the plaintiff changed the above request 1 to: Request the court to declare invalid the minimum top-up amount limit clause formulated by the defendant.

Defendant Tongfang CNKI argued: 1. The balance of individual users' top-ups can be refunded. The customer service representative's reply indicated that a refund was possible, but merely explained that the refund procedure was complicated and a handling fee would be deducted, and suggested that the plaintiff continue using the service. The plaintiff's claim of multiple communications with customer service is untrue. In fact, after learning of the plaintiff's lawsuit, the defendant repeatedly contacted the plaintiff proactively to resolve the matter, but was refused by the plaintiff. The defendant has already refunded 41 yuan from the plaintiff's account balance to the plaintiff's payment account. 2. Article 19 of the Help Center on the website homepage is expressed in a Q&A format and is not prominently placed; it should not be regarded as a contract clause between the parties. In actual operation, the defendant did not follow the provision of that Q&A but allowed refunds of top-up balances. The defendant deleted that Q&A on November 26, 2018. 3. The minimum top-up amount limit is a business practice. The defendant provides various top-up methods on its CNKI website and mobile CNKI, such as Alipay, WeChat Pay, UnionPay Online, membership cards, etc. Some top-up methods have a minimum limit of 10 yuan. Bank wire transfer, postal remittance, and subscription to journals in the book and journal supermarket allow settlement of any amount without a minimum limit. The minimum limits and tiered top-up amounts set for different top-up methods are intended for user efficiency, as this can significantly reduce the number of payment operations per article. After all, most users repeatedly download or read documents, and this method has been recognized by users over many years. Recognizing the practical demand for small payments, the defendant will soon add a payment option of 0.5 yuan via SMS top-up, with a fee of 0.5 yuan per page per document. A minimum top-up of 0.5 yuan is effectively equivalent to canceling the minimum top-up amount limit. In addition, the defendant is also developing a single-article payment system, which is currently being tested.

The Gusu District People's Court of Suzhou, Jiangsu Province, found the following facts in the first instance:

On May 9, 2017, Liu Zhichao topped up 50 yuan via Alipay on CNKI (www.cnki.net) operated by Tongfang CNKI. The CNKI Top-Up Center set the minimum top-up limit for Alipay at 50 yuan. Subsequently, from the date of top-up to June 2, 2018, Liu Zhichao spent a total of 9 yuan on CNKI, leaving an account balance of 41 yuan. On October 21, 2018, Liu Zhichao contacted CNKI customer service by phone and inquired whether custom top-ups were possible and whether the account balance could be refunded. Customer service replied that custom top-ups were not allowed and different top-up methods had different minimum top-up amount provisions. The excess amount could be refunded, but the refund period would be long and a certain handling fee would be deducted. If he wished to continue using CNKI, it was recommended not to request a refund for the time being. On November 6, 2018, Liu Zhichao sued Tongfang CNKI in the Gusu District People's Court of Suzhou, alleging that the minimum top-up amount limit and the provision that the account balance could not be refunded infringed upon his rights. On November 26, 2018, Tongfang CNKI refunded the balance of 41 yuan to Liu Zhichao's Alipay account.

It was further found that the CNKI Top-Up Center listed various top-up methods: Alipay, WeChat Pay, UnionPay Online, membership cards, Shenzhouxing cards, Huifu Tianxia, mobile SMS, bank wire transfer, postal remittance, etc. Among them, the minimum top-up limit for Alipay was 50 yuan, and some other payment methods also set different minimum top-up amount limits. In the "Answers to Readers" section of the Help Center page on CNKI, Article 19 stated: "Can the unused amount of an individual user be unsubscribed? The account balance does not support the transfer-out function. The purchased top-up amount has no time limit and must be used up." After Liu Zhichao filed the lawsuit, Tongfang CNKI deleted this Q&A content.

The Gusu District People's Court of Suzhou, Jiangsu Province, held in the first instance:

Consumers have the right to freely choose goods or services, to independently select the type or mode of goods or services, and to decide whether to purchase or not to purchase any kind of goods. Operators shall not, by way of standard terms, notices, declarations, shop notices, etc., make provisions that exclude or restrict consumers' rights, reduce or exempt operators' liabilities, increase consumers' responsibilities, or are otherwise unfair or unreasonable to consumers, nor shall they use standard terms and technical means to compel transactions. Standard terms, notices, declarations, shop notices, etc., containing the content listed in the preceding paragraph shall be invalid. In this case, the defendant Tongfang CNKI's provision on the minimum top-up amount limit on CNKI caused consumers to be required to top up a minimum of 10 to 50 yuan to purchase a document costing only a few yuan. Although the account balance could be refunded, Tongfang CNKI stated that a handling fee would be deducted for refunds. Therefore, the setting of the minimum top-up amount occupied consumers' excess funds, and charging a handling fee for refunds also increased consumers' burden. Accordingly, this provision infringed upon consumers' right to free choice, restricted consumers' rights, and was an unfair and unreasonable provision for consumers, and should be deemed invalid. Although the minimum top-up amount in this case was relatively low and most consumers could tolerate it without objection, the negative demonstration effect of this practice should still be taken seriously and be regulated and guided. Merchants should allow consumers to customize the top-up amount when topping up. As for Liu Zhichao's request for Tongfang CNKI to refund the money, since Tongfang CNKI had already made the refund, this request was dismissed.

In conclusion, the Gusu District People's Court of Suzhou, in accordance with Article 9, Article 26, paragraphs 2 and 3 of the Law on the Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests of the People's Republic of China, and Article 271 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment on January 30, 2019:

1. The provision on the minimum top-up amount limit set by the defendant Tongfang CNKI (Beijing) Technology Co., Ltd. in its CNKI (www.cnki.net) Top-Up Center is invalid.

2. All other claims of Liu Zhichao are dismissed.

This judgment is final.
